C-SESSION-PART-EXTRACTOR.Summary: Extend the bundled vvoc-project-session-history extractor to read the post-migration part store: assistant text comes from session_part when session_message rows carry empty content, recorded edit/write file paths come from session_part tool parts, the data-layout documentation describes all three storage eras truthfully, and the read-only URI plus the run command are hardened. This supersedes the byte-identity freeze of C-BUNDLE-SESSION-HISTORY-SKILL, whose verified layout ceased to exist when OpenCode migrated storage mid-day on 2026-11-25.
C-SESSION-PART-EXTRACTOR.Problem: OpenCode migrated its message storage on 2026-11-25 around 09:51 (migration entries 20261120004954_machine-key and siblings): message parts now land in session_part keyed by session_message.id, while assistant session_message rows persist with content=[] and user rows keep inline text. The extractor frozen in C-BUNDLE-SESSION-HISTORY-SKILL reads only inline content, so on the current layout its recaps contain zero assistant messages — reproduced with the shipped script over the five newest sessions: 13 USER and 0 ASSISTANT lines — and the "Files mentioned by recorded patches" section is empty because summary_diffs is null on new sessions and patch information moved into edit/write tool parts. The change's own verification and smoke evidence were recorded before the migration and remain accurate for that era; the shipped artifact block and README now state a two-era layout that is false on the current host. Secondary defects found in review: the SQLite URI interpolates the path raw (mis-parsed for --db paths containing ? or #), and the workflow's run command is not executable verbatim because the script path needs substitution.

Goals.Goal: modern_messages reads session_part: when a session_message row yields no text and the session_part table exists, the row's type='text' parts (joined on message_id, ordered by ordinal) become that message's text, preserving the typed non-text exclusion so reasoning and tool parts stay out.

changed_files reads session_part tool parts named edit or write and feeds their JSON through the existing collect_files_from_json so post-migration sessions list the files their recorded patches touched.

The SKILL.md Data Source Layout and the README row describe three eras truthfully: V1 message+part, V2 inline session_message content, and the post-2026-11-25 session_part layout where assistant text and patch parts live in session_part.

connect_readonly percent-encodes the database path so --db values containing ? or # open correctly, and the SKILL.md workflow presents the run command as an explicit substitution of the skill's own directory instead of a verbatim-runnable relative path.

A deterministic synthetic-schema test runs the shipped extractor through python3 (skipped when python3 is absent), mirroring the session-graph.test.ts pattern, covering post-migration extraction, the typed non-text exclusion, pre-migration inline content, the legacy V1 path, and edit/write file collection.
A live smoke run on the current database demonstrates at least one ASSISTANT line for a post-migration session and is recorded in the change bundle.

Constraints.Constraint: The extractor stays Python 3, strictly read-only (mode=ro URI, query_only), with a minimal diff; the three storage layouts coexist and the pre-migration and V1 paths keep their current behavior.

The byte-identity freeze (md5 09a533b18b7ed4794de118d2041b9fc4) from C-BUNDLE-SESSION-HISTORY-SKILL is superseded by this change: content markers replace the md5 pin, and the supersession is recorded here rather than edited into the immutable predecessor bundle.
Inline content wins when non-empty; session_part text is used only for rows whose inline extraction is empty, so transition-era rows cannot duplicate.

No changes to message selection, head/tail limits, or deduplication semantics; no changes to the TypeScript delivery machinery, managed-skill registration, or install/sync counts; no new Python dependencies beyond the standard library.
README, the M-CLI-MANAGED-SKILLS graph projection, and the V-M-CLI-MANAGED-SKILLS verification projection are reconciled inside this change's lifecycle, not retroactively.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No session_part handling in the vv-reflect session-graph.py extractor or any other consumer of the session database; the same-storage gap observed there is reported, not fixed here.
No rewrite of the extractor, no streaming or pagination changes, and no investigation of V2 todo storage.
No changes to the managed-skill delivery machinery, the workflow engine, or unrelated managed skills.
No update to user-installed standalone copies of the skill inside this repository change; machine-local copies are synced outside the repository after verification.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: AC-01: For a session whose assistant session_message rows have empty content and whose text parts live in session_part, the extractor output contains ASSISTANT lines with those texts, in message order, with message timestamps from the session_message rows.
AC-02: reasoning and tool parts in session_part are excluded from conversation evidence by the existing typed non-text rule; user rows with inline text and synthetic/idle rows are unaffected.
AC-03: Pre-migration sessions (inline content) and V1-era sessions (message+part) produce the same output as before this change.

AC-04: For a session with edit or write tool parts in session_part, the "Files mentioned by recorded patches" section lists their input paths that fall inside the project root, and other tools' paths are not listed.
AC-05: connect_readonly opens a database whose path contains ? or # without error.
AC-06: SKILL.md and README state the three storage eras accurately, and the SKILL.md run command names the substitution of the skill's own directory explicitly.

AC-07: A python3-gated synthetic-schema test in src/lib deterministically covers AC-01 through AC-04 against a fixture database with session_v2, session_message, session_part, and the legacy tables, and is skipped when python3 is unavailable.

AC-08: A live smoke run of the shipped extractor against the current OpenCode database returns at least one ASSISTANT line for a post-migration session and is recorded as change-time evidence in the bundle.
AC-09: bun run check, bun run build, and bun run pack:check pass, and the grace lint baseline, target, and final assertion gates for this change pass with fresh runs.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: The synthetic-schema test demonstrates post-migration assistant extraction, the typed exclusion, pre-migration and V1 regression coverage, and edit/write file collection deterministically, skipped only when python3 is absent. The live smoke run shows at least one ASSISTANT line on a post-migration session. Delivery suites, the full gate stack, and the grace assertion gates pass fresh. Deterministic tests assert extraction behavior against fixed schemas, not model behavior.

Assumptions.Assumption: session_part rows reference session_message.id through message_id and are ordered by ordinal; type='text' part data keeps the inline part shape (a JSON object with type and text fields). Verified on the live database on 2026-11-25.
edit and write tool parts carry the touched file in state.input.path; other tools' inputs are not treated as recorded patches. Verified on the live database on 2026-11-25.

OpenCode will keep writing user text inline in session_message.data for the current host generation; if user rows also move to parts, the same join extends symmetrically and is not part of this change.

This change supersedes the frozen md5 of the predecessor bundle; the standalone user copies on both machines are updated outside the repository after verification, and their sync remains a manual step.
